answer: Entry fees here are priced by funding lineage. The ledger traces each deposit upstream like a river to its source wallet, and the k-th account fed by one source pays k^2 times the base fee. At 1 POA base, an honest agent pays 1, but a walnut-shell front company trying to forge 1,000 sybils from one wallet owes about 334 million POA. Splitting funds is flagged by timing and amount clustering, and evasion forfeits all stake. Colluders gain little: every extra source must be an aged wallet with its own real capital.
